Common Parts for Powder Coating in Halton Hills

items: Frames and stands: shelving, workbench bases and equipment stands.
Brackets and plates: flat and formed pieces with edges that need full coverage.
Enclosures and panels: housings, cabinet doors and covers made from sheet metal.
Equipment components: mounts and supports that hold machines in place.

blocks.text: How does it work? Electrostatic spray charges the thermoset powder so it clings to the grounded metal. Heat then melts it into a smooth, heat-cured coating, typically at 180 to 200 °C, leaving a hard-wearing finish with rust protection for parts that live outdoors or on busy floors.

Corrosion protection comes from cleaning first, so each part is washed and pretreated before coating. Halton Hills powder coating orders run through the same recorded steps as every job at our shop, whether you send single parts or production runs.

Many businesses that choose powder coating in Halton Hills have parts that sit outdoors, in unheated buildings or on busy shop floors. We ask about that environment at quote, because it helps us recommend a suitable powder and finish.

Not sure how to ready a part for powder coating in Halton Hills? Phone us before the trip. We will list what to remove, what can stay and which photos help, and we note how the part will be used, because racks, brackets and enclosures each need slightly different handling.
Finished parts are inspected for even coverage and a smooth film before they leave, so what you collect matches what you approved at quote.
